title: Journey fact snapshots and sparse indexes for Console analytics
creator: Ava Patel
description: Create a set of compact, query-friendly journey fact tables and periodic snapshot materializations for Console usage analytics. The goal is to support low-latency funnel queries, cohorting by feature usage, and cost-attribution reports without scanning high-volume event streams. This ticket covers schema design, sparse indexing strategy for high-cardinality attributes, incremental materialization jobs, and migration steps from ad-hoc denorm views to curated tables.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A set of 3 fact tables (journey_event_facts, session_summary_facts, route_cohort_snapshots) created in the warehouse with documented schemas and partitioning strategy.
2) Incremental materialization jobs running daily and backfill completed for last 90 days.
3) Query performance: representative funnel queries return in < 6s on standard analytics cluster and cost < 40% of baseline ad-hoc SQL.
4) Dashboard owners (Growth, Console PM) validate results against existing dashboards and sign off.
5) Rollout plan to switch dashboards to new tables with traffic split and rollback plan documented.
implementation_plan: Design schemas for three tables with explicit primary keys and surrogate ids (journey_event_facts, session_summary_facts, route_cohort_snapshots).
Choose partitioning: daily ingestion partitions for facts, month partitions for snapshots; cluster by (org_id, route_hash) where query patterns warrant.
Apply sparse indexing on high-cardinality string attributes (route, feature_flag, model_variant) using hashed prefix columns to enable fast equality filters.
Implement dedupe and canonicalization logic in ingestion layer: deterministic event hashing, earliest event per token rules, and TTL for stale KV entries.
Build incremental materialization Airflow/DBT job with CDC-friendly upsert pattern and fast-path insert for new partitions.
Create backfill job for last 90 days with quota-aware batching and cost caps; perform dry run on staging.
Add CI checks: schema test, row-count diff thresholds, and value sanity checks (e.g., sessions per user < 200).
Coordinate rollout: cutover dashboards to snapshots with 10/30/60/100% switch and a 24-hour monitoring window.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Create tables in analytics dev schema and run validation backfills. Phase 2: Run parallel queries (new tables vs denorm views) for 7 days, capture diffs, and iterate. Phase 3: Schedule staged cutover on weekend with runbook: disable ad-hoc writes to denorm views, switch dashboard data sources, monitor SLOs, and revert if >5% discrepancy or error spike. Phase 4: Decommission old denorm views once stable for 14 days.
testing_plan: Unit tests for dbt models + integration tests against staging parquet snapshots. Performance tests: execute 10 representative queries and record p95 latency and bytes scanned. End-to-end validation by Console product analytics: sign-off and sample-based row-level equality checks. Add alerts for materialization failures and drift detection on row counts.
risks:
1) High-cardinality columns may still cause wide scans even with sparse indexes — mitigated by hashed prefix columns and sampling.
2) Backfill cost and quota exhaustion — mitigated by rate-limited batching and per-org throttling.
3) Slight numeric drift vs denorm views due to sessionization cutpoints — requires alignment of sessionization window logic and explicit regression tests.
4) Rollout may surface downstream dashboard assumptions (e.g., implicit filters) — include dashboard owners in validation.
metrics: Primary signals: p95 query latency for funnel queries, bytes scanned per query, daily job runtime, and monthly compute cost for Console analytics. Success thresholds: p95 latency < 6s, bytes scanned down 50% vs baseline, daily job runtime < 90 minutes for full incremental, backfill cost within budget cap.
